CONDITION: EXPERIMENT
STARTING HYPOTHESIS: The strongest fit will be a harness-level adaptation system rather than generic long-term memory: repeated failures, reusable tactics and recurring delegation patterns should flow from trajectory review into typed durable memories, skills and subagent specifications, those artifacts should affect later agent context/behavior, and refinement history plus real snapshot/version rollback should make bad adaptations reversible. A repository that merely writes notes or lets a user hand-author skills is insufficient.
DISCOVERY METHODS: (1) direct domain/problem search across persistent self-improving agent harnesses, continual adaptation, durable memory/skills/subagents and rollback; (2) code/signature search for typed refinement kinds, auto-refine gates, refinement history, before/after snapshots, version counters, rollback IDs, stale-plan rejection and session/global scope; (3) paper-to-code/production-descendant tracing from the Continual Harness research line into a maintained production-oriented implementation; (4) adversarial ecosystem comparison against Hermes Agent, OmniHarness, agent-execution-harness and self-improving-skills to separate skill-only/memory-only adaptation from a typed whole-harness loop.
CANDIDATE: Prime Agent — Continual Harness
CANONICAL URL: https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent
EXACT REVISION: e311d6495124cf0bdc629c813fc97a39a9a3054d
VERDICT: STRONG
A-F SCORE: A4 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E5 / F4 = 28/30. The requested persistent adaptation/rollback mechanics are implemented and unusually well tested; operational/security caveats and the distinction between refining a skill contract versus synthesizing a brand-new executable skill package cap deployment clarity.
EVIDENCE INSPECTED: DISCOVERY/PAPER-LINEAGE pass traced the 2026 Continual Harness research concept into Prime Agent's maintained production-oriented repository; CODE INSPECTOR inspected `packages/coding-agent/src/core/refinement/refinement.ts`, `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`, the `refine` and `skill-creator` built-in skills, and settings for automatic refinement; TEST/SCHEMA INSPECTOR inspected `packages/coding-agent/test/refinement.test.ts` and `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-serialized-refine.test.ts`, including typed CRUD/versioning, stale-plan rejection, persisted apply, automatic turn-threshold refinement and rollback tests; HISTORY/PROVENANCE VALIDATOR pinned `e311d649...`, inspected recent refinement hardening commits and the MIT license; ECOSYSTEM/COMMERCIAL pass compared Hermes' memory/skill curator plus rollback, OmniHarness and narrower self-improving-skill projects; independent RED-TEAM/VERIFIER challenged whether the artifact types are real, whether automatic refinement changes durable state, whether rollback restores snapshots, and whether 'skill' means executable capability rather than only prose.
CLAIMS VERIFIED: Prime Agent has a persistent Continual Harness with four first-class refinement kinds: `prompt`, `memory`, `skill` and `subagent`. The refinement system prompt explicitly maps durable facts/decisions/failures/outcomes to memory, repeated procedures to skills, and repeated delegation roles to subagent specs, while preserving local-session versus global-cross-session scope. The built-in `refine` skill explicitly says to invoke refinement after a repeated failure, reusable tactic, delegation role or behavior policy; `await refine.run(...)` schedules a trajectory-based review. Automatic refinement is enabled by default, with a configurable assistant-turn interval, compaction trigger and cooldown, and an LLM review gate rejects one-off noise/unsupported hypotheses before planning edits. `HarnessEntry` records kind, content, scope, metadata, timestamps and a monotonically incremented version; `HarnessRefinementEvent` records trigger, changes, evidence, outcome and time; global refinement results are append-only in `refinements.jsonl`, while local refinements are recorded with their session artifact path. The exact-revision test suite runs create/update/delete lifecycles across all four artifact kinds, verifies version 1->2 transitions and before/after snapshots, requires Python reference/argument contracts for skill entries, atomically persists harness state, rejects malformed edits without mutating state/history, and rejects a planned update when the target changed concurrently. Serialized-refinement integration tests verify that real automatic turn-threshold review leads to plan/apply before the next model turn, that an in-flight plan is aborted rather than applied after branch navigation, and that the non-mocked apply path persists a new memory in the local harness. Rollback tests pass a concrete `rollbackId`, assert `rollbackOf`, undo edits in reverse order and restore pre-edit snapshots; local-session isolation is also tested. The built-in skill creator separately supports creating, validating and installing markdown or Python-backed reusable skills, while the RLM runtime supports real spawned subagents. Recent commit history shows active hardening of harness-state fingerprinting, refinement ordering and regression coverage rather than a static research demo. Public license is MIT.
CLAIMS NOT VERIFIED: The runtime does not have a deterministic classifier proving that a particular failure is 'repeated'; semantic selection of what deserves refinement remains model/reviewer judgment. `/refine` can create/update durable skill entries with executable Python call contracts, but the README explicitly says continual-harness refinement does not replace packaging/reviewing new executable skills; the separate skill-creator path is needed to author/install a new skill package, so fully autonomous code-skill synthesis from a failure was not credited. Harness refinement is behavioral/context adaptation, not model-weight learning. Rollback covers recorded harness refinements, not arbitrary external side effects or every action the agent performed. The README explicitly warns that the worker/kernel isolation is not a security sandbox. Independent enterprise deployment evidence, measured reliability lift and ROI from continual refinement were not verified.
STRONGEST OBJECTION: 'Self-improving agent' is easy to overstate. Prime Agent genuinely persists and revises typed memories, skill contracts and subagent specifications with history and rollback, but the quality of what gets learned is still LLM-mediated, and a refined skill entry is not automatically a newly packaged executable tool. The independent verifier therefore calls the repository STRONG for the benchmark's persistent-harness/rollback requirement while refusing stronger claims about autonomous code synthesis, weight learning or sandboxed production safety.
COMMERCIAL WEDGE: A governed agent-reliability layer for engineering/research teams running long-lived agents: capture project-specific failures, successful procedures and recurring delegation patterns into reviewable local/global harness artifacts, expose the refinement ledger and before/after versions to operators, and let teams roll back bad adaptations. The smallest paid wedge is an 'agent memory and operating-playbook audit' for an existing coding/research-agent deployment, followed by managed team-wide refinement policies and reusable project skills/subagent roles. The money path is reduced repeated rediscovery, fewer recurrent agent mistakes, faster onboarding of new agent sessions and auditable reversal when learned guidance degrades performance.
SEARCH EFFORT: 12 materially distinct discovery/lineage/signature searches and 11 deep source/test/history/comparator inspections; specialist passes: discovery, paper/lineage validator, code inspector, test/schema/history validator, ecosystem/commercial analyst and independent RED-TEAM/VERIFIER.
FALSE-PROMOTION RISK: Moderate. README phrases such as 'self-improving', 'skills are executable' and 'subagents are built in' could be conflated into a stronger autonomous-skill-synthesis claim than the code proves. Promotion is justified only for the narrower verified loop: trajectory review -> typed durable harness edit -> persisted/versioned state -> later harness delivery -> refinement history -> snapshot rollback, with explicit tests for artifact lifecycle, stale-plan rejection and rollback.
LESSON: For self-improving-agent searches, use a HARNESS-ARTIFACT CLOSED-LOOP test: trace `trajectory signal/review -> typed durable artifact -> persisted version/history -> next-session or next-turn delivery/use -> rollback/negative control`, and verify memory, skill and delegation/subagent artifacts independently. Do not credit generic memory, a manual skill authoring command, or a 'self-improving' label unless the adaptation path actually mutates reusable state and bad refinements are reversible. This is the first benchmark confirmation of this specific skill, so keep it candidate-only.

EVIDENCE-BACKED LESSONS:
- Task 28 independently reinforces DECISION-CLAIM -> RUNTIME-SIDE-EFFECT TRACE in an adaptation setting: a self-improvement claim counted only after tracing trajectory review through the automatic/manual refine gate into a typed harness mutation, persistence/version history, and tests that later state actually contains the edit. README-level 'self-improving' language was not sufficient.
- FAILED SEARCH PATTERN: Generic `self-improving agent`, `long-term memory`, `skills` and `subagents` searches surface many projects with only one or two of the required artifact classes. Skill-only self-editors and memory stores are components, not a whole persistent harness, unless repeated experience can mutate multiple reusable artifact types and the mutation is auditable/reversible.
- USEFUL SIGNATURES: `RefinementKind = prompt|memory|skill|subagent`, `HarnessEntry.version`, `HarnessRefinementEvent`, `refinements.jsonl`, `rollbackId`/`rollbackOf`, before/after snapshots, stale-planning conflict rejection, local/global harness scope, auto-refine review thresholds, and tests that execute create/update/delete across every artifact kind.
- BAD ASSUMPTION: A durable 'skill' entry is not automatically proof of autonomous executable-skill synthesis. Prime Agent's `/refine` can persist a skill contract/reference, while its own README says new executable skill packaging/review remains a separate concern; keep those capabilities distinct.
- CANDIDATE SEARCH SKILL — HARNESS-ARTIFACT CLOSED LOOP: For persistent self-improving agents, require `trajectory signal/review -> typed reusable artifact -> durable version/history -> later delivery/use -> rollback or negative-control test`. Verify memory, skill and subagent/delegation artifacts separately. Task 28 is the first benchmark confirmation; do not promote to SEARCH_SKILLS until a second distinct task or Hunt 15 approval.
